8. Approved ROE 
In determining a reasonable ROE, the Authority considers the analytical models 
for commensurate utility returns, allowed ROEs in other jurisdictions, the prevailing 
market conditions, and the Company’s risk profile.  The Authority considers the two 
analytical models (DCF and CAPM) to provide a target range for commensurate ROEs.  
The Authority generally weighs the DCF model results more heavily than the CAPM 
results because the DCF model relies on directly observable proxy company market data 
and provides a better measure of the COE for similarly situated utilities.  Conversely, the 
CAPM relies primarily on risk-premium studies and market predictions, which are more 
subjective in nature. 
Here, the DCF model as applied to the Authority Proxy Group indicates an ROE 
range of 8.57% to 10.29%, with an average of 9.44%.  The CAPM model produced an 
ROE range of 7.65% to 9.35%, with an average of 8.50%.  Given the Authority’s weighting 
of these models, the data indicates that an ROE between 8.5% and 10.0% would be 
sufficient to provide a reasonable, market-based return. 
Given this range, the Authority must determine an ROE such that the Company 
has an opportunity to “cover . . . [its] capital costs, to attract needed capital and to maintain 
[its] financial integrity.”  General Statutes § 16-19e(a)(4).  This statutory standard reflects 
the long-standing principle that “the return to the equity owner should be commensurate 
with returns on investments in other enterprises having corresponding risks and should 
also be sufficient to assure confidence in the financial integrity of the enterprise, so as to 
maintain its credit and to attract capital.”  Connecticut Light & Power Co. v. Dept. of Public 
Utility Control, 216 Conn. at 634–35.  In determining an ROE, the Authority “is not bound 
to the use of any single formula or combination of formulae” but again must balance 
“investor and consumer interests” and make “pragmatic adjustments.”  Woodbury Water 
Co., 174 Conn. at 264. 
Cognizant of this legal framework, the Authority has analyzed a wide array of 
considerations in reaching a determination, including, without limitation, the Company’s 
capital structure, its financial condition, ROEs from other jurisdictions, analytical models 
of commensurate returns, prevailing and anticipated market conditions, risk factors, and 
the regulatory environment. 
The Company is financially stable, maintaining an A Rating from S&P, an A2 rating 
from Moody’s, and an A- rating from Fitch.  In addition, the Company operates in a 
regulatory environment that reduces risk through the Distribution Integrity Management 
Program (DIMP) mechanism and the revenue decoupling adjustment.  Considering these 
and other factors, the Authority adopts a 9.20% ROE.  Accounting for the 5 basis point 
reduction, the Authority approves a 9.15% ROE.

current approved return on equity is 9.3%.  Under the Plan, this number is adjusted annually

creating a balanced set of risks and rewards that drive utility performance.  For example,

investigation into Vermont Gas Systems, Inc.’s (“Vermont Gas” or the “Company”) tariff filing

determine that a 10.13% increase for non-gas costs should be approved effective for bills

On February 15, 2023, Vermont Gas filed a petition requesting a 10.7% increase in non-

effectiveness of the proposed tariffs pursuant to Section 226(a) with implementation occurring

unamortized debt expenses from rate base at an ROE of 9.34% would reduce Vermont Gas’s

II.

On February 14, 2020, Vermont Gas filed the petition and proposed tariffs reflecting an 
overall 2.9% increase in rates that would be implemented on a bills-rendered basis beginning on

FINDINGS 
1. On February 14, 2020, Vermont Gas filed a Petition seeking approval to implement a 
3% increase to base rates and to return $5.58 million to customers from the System Expansion

pf. at 3.
